observationsNotFindings: The D9 handling across this chain is the thing most likely to go wrong and it holds at every layer. v15 already records the golden and states in terms that it mints no new code or exit number; the FC-OUTFAIL bind quotes that sentence exactly and attributes the exit value 4 to d9-exit-contract v1.14 rather than supplying it; and the subject contains no 4 at all. The FC-NONAUTH-TERM bind goes further and refuses even to choose which D9 a renderer attempts, which is the right line for a negative test about renderer authority.

The bind-versus-bytes split is a genuinely useful distinction and this is the first artifact in the sweep to draw it. A bind states exact-byte intent for a named case without supplying bytes; the bytes remain leftover. That lets FC-OUTFAIL and FC-NONAUTH-TERM stop being undifferentiated leftover without anyone pretending fixtures exist. The two -FX obligations carry the remainder honestly.

The specifiedNotLeftover bucket now holds five obligations of three different kinds: specified inside v15, a table authored elsewhere, and two binds authored elsewhere. I raised the flattening at v2 as an uncharged observation and it has grown rather than shrunk. Still not a finding, since every reason names where its artifact lives, but a bucket that groups contract-specified law with three separately authored artifacts is doing less work than its name suggests.

Provenance is the standing concern and it has deepened. Seven review pins, one Codex. DR-122's design standing now rests on a three-deep stack of Claude-only acceptances - advertisement table, then v2, then v3 - with two further Claude-only binds beneath. Every artifact discloses 'Codex not reviewed' honestly and no single one overstates, but the aggregate is only visible from the coordinator's position.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The delta is exact: nothing dropped, seven obligations object-identical to v2, two new -FX obligations, and exactly the two the dispatch names flipping from leftover-design to specified-not-leftover. The sharpest prohibition here is the D9 code, and it holds at every layer. I read both binds directly rather than trusting their verdicts or the subject's description of them: the FC-OUTFAIL bind binds to the already-recorded D9 v1.14 golden and reproduces live v15's ownerOfValues sentence exactly under ==, including its own statement that it mints no new code or exit number; the FC-NONAUTH-TERM bind refuses even to choose which D9 a renderer attempts. I chased the exit value 4 in particular, since a minted exit number would have been a blocker - it traces to d9-exit-contract v1.14 via v15's own behavior text, and the subject contains no 4 at all. All four named cases across the two binds carry fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED, which is what the two -FX obligations rest on, so the bind-versus-bytes split is real rather than a relabelling. All 19 recordedInputs and fifteen pins recompute with zero mismatches, fixtureClassesVerbatim equals live v15, the token is correctly PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, and D-152's historical cardinality is not imported. Two standing notes rather than findings: the specifiedNotLeftover bucket now holds five obligations of three different kinds, which I first flagged at v2 and which has grown; and provenance has deepened - seven review pins with one Codex, three of the Claude pins mine, and DR-122 now resting on a three-deep stack of Claude-only acceptances. Nothing is misstated and every single-reviewer pin says so, but the aggregate is visible only from the coordinator's position. 21 attacks run, 21 refuted, with the circularity refuted as to the bytes and disclosed as to the verdicts.
